newsitem.title: USA: US spot natgas still supported by SW heat, outages.
newsitem.headline: US spot natgas still supported by SW heat, outages.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices wavered only slightly Thursday as moderate weather continued in the East and upper Midwest and heat still blanketed the Southwest, industry sources said.

On the Louisiana Gulf Coast, prices were quoted about one cent lower at $2.13-2.16 per mmBtu at the Henry Hub, pressured by cool weather in the East and an unexpectedly high injection rate as reported by the American Gas Asscociation.
Conversely, Permian prices edged about one cent higher to about $2.06-2.07 due to 100-degree temperatures in Arizona and plant outages.

AGA reported Wednesday that gas stocks were up 96 bcf, climbing to 222 bcf, or 15 percent, above year-ago tallies. Despite the large build, western stocks continued to lag seven percent below year-ago levels.
Southern California border prices were up an equal amount to about $2.25-2.26.
The outage list in the West continued to grow as the 750 megawatt (MW) Navajo 1 coal unit in Arizona was set to shut Friday night through Monday morning for repairs, the plant reported today.
The 750 MW unit 5 at the Four Corners coal plant in New Mexico is also expected to shut Friday for three weeks for repairs.
Southern California Edison's 750 MW Mohave 2 coal unit in Nevada remained off line and no estimate on when the unit would restart was yet available.
Also, the 1,080 MW San Onofre 2 nuclear unit in California was expected to remain off line until late next week.
The adjacent unit 3, with a generating capacity of 1,080 MW, was slated to restart Saturday, according to the company.
In the East, swing prices at the New York city-gate held in the high-$2.30s as moderate weather in the region continued to keep a lid on cooling demand.
In the Midwest, swing prices were steady to down about one cent to about $2.03. Chicago city-gate prices were quoted equally softer around $2.18.
